mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, which raises the cost of capital and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 5% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.0% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and lowers profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which erodes real purchasing power and increases discount rates, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL > 202.0 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in housing starts (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market gains over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates population reclassification or labor force re-entry without job creation, which weakens wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases AND UNRATE increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which dampens demand for equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
